a_explore_sweep.gpx.desc: (a) Garmin Explore (creator -> deviceLogger), train ~40 m/s, true 1 Hz with 1-4 points per second-resolution stamp. Fix lost 1778916118..1778916478 (stamped): the app re-emits its stored last 3 km (77 fixes, bit-identical strings) as a triangle sweep starting at the oldest fix (2994 m back), 1 fix/s = 40 m/s, ~75 s per pass, 360 replay records; then live resumes 15115 m away. Accepted outcomes (spec): replayFlags marks >= 60% of the 360 replay records (only they can match, so <= 360) and the sweep vanishes from the jitter scan (jitter 0 is fine), OR jitter covers it -> jitter range 0..3, no jitter_cover. gaps exactly 0: no step has dt >= 20 s and stamps never jump >= 5 s, so the staleClock search cannot find a clock jump. No cluster may start in the clean live parts.

a2_explore_sawtooth_perturbed.gpx.desc: (a variant) same loss 1779002519..1779002878, but each pass restarts at the oldest stored fix (3 km reversal every 77 s: 5 restarts incl. the first) and every replayed fix is moved 1-2 m (not bit-identical) -> replays 0. This is the shape the 90 s merge window was designed for: one reversal cluster per restart, consecutive clusters ~75 s apart merge into one that spans at least first restart..last restart (300 of 360 s, IoU ~0.83 with the loss interval). The final forward jump to the live position is not a reversal, so it may or may not add a cluster -> jitter 1..2.

g_explore_sweep_perturbed.gpx.desc: (g) the (a) triangle sweep (1779088919..1779089278) with every replayed coordinate moved 1-2 m -> replays 0 (nothing bit-identical). Spec: a jitter cluster must be present. The sweep starts with a 2988 m reversal (oldest stored fix) which opens a cluster; the triangle turn-arounds themselves are gradual (40 m per fix) and the passes run at the train speed, so full coverage of the 6 min is NOT expected from per-step jump/reversal tests -> jitter 1..4, no jitter_cover.

b_phone_interleave.csv.desc: (b) phone CSV (accuracy column -> phone), regional train ~35 m/s at 1 Hz. 1780364400..1780364700 the source alternates every 1-3 s between the live fix and a bit-identical copy of the fix from 40 s earlier (1.4 km behind): 148 delayed records, of which 89 copy a fix that was itself written (the others copy a moment when the delayed stream was being written, so they match nothing). Those 89 are textbook replays (40 s old, track 1.4 km away in between, moving) -> replays >= 90% of 89, <= 89. The unflagged delayed records still alternate with the live ones, so a jitter cluster must cover the 5 min (IoU >= 0.5); 1..3 clusters allowed (90 s merge).

b2_phone_interleave_requant.csv.desc: (b variant) same interleave 1780450800..1780451100 (148 delayed records) but the delayed stream writes its coordinates at 5 decimals, so nothing is bit-identical -> replays 0 and the whole job falls to detectJitter: 1.4 km reversals every 1-3 s for 5 min -> cluster(s) covering it (IoU >= 0.5).

c_tunnel_pingpong.csv.desc: (c) phone 1 Hz, car ~25 m/s in a tunnel: 1783155900..1783156020 (120 s, 120 records, no time hole) the fixes alternate (runs of 1-3) between two network positions 926 m apart (tunnel entry and 1 km further), each with ~12 m scatter (not bit-identical -> replays 0); the car meanwhile drives 3 km. Exactly one cluster covering the ping-pong (IoU >= 0.5). Phone profile -> staleClock off, no dt >= 20 s -> gaps 0.

c2_tunnel_pingpong_cellfix.csv.desc: (c variant) as (c) 1783242300..1783242420 but the two positions are fixed strings: P = the last live fix (cached), Q = one cell position 926 m ahead. Ping-pong points ~10 s after a visit to the other spot satisfy every replay criterion, the rest do not, so the split between replayFlags and detectJitter depends on the visit order -> wide ranges: replays 0..120, jitter 0..2; only no-crash, invariants and no clusters in the clean parts are firm.

c3_tunnel_pingpong_x5.csv.desc: (c variant) the (c) tunnel ping-pong five times in one 1 h drive (other noise draws), 10 min of clean driving between tunnels so nothing merges: 1783321500..1783321620, 1783322220..1783322340, 1783322940..1783323060, 1783323660..1783323780, 1783324380..1783324500. Each tunnel must get exactly one cluster covering it (IoU >= 0.5) -> jitter exactly 5; none may start in the clean parts. Same physics as (c), but five independent draws, so a pass/fail here does not hinge on one seed.

d_cochem_dr_overshoot.csv.desc: (d) phone 1 Hz, RE at 33 m/s into the Kaiser-Wilhelm-Tunnel at 1786270300; in the tunnel the phone dead-reckons smoothly at the entry speed while the train brakes, at 1786270410 the fix returns and the position snaps back 956 m (true overshoot 957 m), then a 90 s station stop. The DR stretch is smooth and indistinguishable step by step; the snap is a ~1 km reversal -> 1 cluster at the snap (A = DR tip, B = first real fix); a second one is tolerated -> jitter 1..2, and no cluster may start before the tunnel or after the snap (location check without assuming whether a future detector also claims the DR stretch). Ground-truth garbage: 1786270300..1786270410.

e_outlier_lateral.gpx.desc: (e) eTrex (creator -> deviceLogger), car 18-25 m/s on a winding road at a steady 1 Hz; the single fix at 1789200600 is 2 km to the LEFT of the road (out and straight back). Spec: exactly one cluster A = 1789200599 .. B = 1789200601 (chord 45 m = two normal steps, i.e. noise level). No clock jump at 1 Hz -> no staleClock; replays 0.

e2_outlier_behind.gpx.desc: (e variant) as (e) but the single fix at 1789287000 lies 2 km BEHIND the car (a 2 km reversal and back) -> exactly one cluster 1789286999..1789287001 (chord 51 m).

f_station_cached_replay.csv.desc: (f) phone 1 Hz, train 30 m/s with two stops without fix. Stop 1 1781916660..1781916960: 4 cached approach fixes (spread 105 m, hops up to 105 m, bit-identical strings) re-emitted for 300 s - repeats are >= 10 s apart and some hops pass the 50 m moving test, but the track never departs 300 m from them -> not replays. Stop 2 1781917380..1781917560: the last fix repeated for 180 s (neighbour 10 s earlier is the same spot -> not moving). 480 cached records in all -> replays exactly 0. Largest step in the whole file 106 m < the 200 m reversal floor -> jitter exactly 0.

h_sweep_10s.csv.desc: (h) phone CSV at a fixed 10 s interval, train ~40 m/s (400 m per sample). 1790994000..1790994360: 36 replay records sweeping the stored last 3 km (8 fixes, bit-identical, triangle from the oldest). Visits to the newest stored fix equal the last live fix position, so they fail the 50 m moving test; every other replay record is moving, >= 10 s after its original and separated by a >= 300 m departure -> replays >= 60% of 36. As in (a) either outcome is acceptable for the jitter scan -> 0..2. 10 s steps, phone -> gaps 0.

i_hole_then_pingpong.csv.desc: (i) phone 1 Hz, car ~25 m/s: no records 1783751699..1783751740 (40 s, ~1 km driven), then immediately 1783751740..1783751830 ping-pong between the true position after the hole and a network fix 765 m back. The step over the hole is a timeGap (~1 km / 40 s, ~90 km/h); ping-pong steps are 1 s so they are never timeGaps and staleClock is off for phones -> gaps exactly 1. The ping-pong starts right after a hole, i.e. with an empty jitter reference window -> jitter 0..3 (no firm claim); candidates (gaps + kept jitter) 1..4. No cluster in the clean parts.

j_long_pingpong.csv.desc: (j) phone 1 Hz, train ~30 m/s: 20 min (1788059100..1788060300, 1200 records) of continuous ping-pong between two noisy fixes 1199 m apart, no time hole. Longer than the 600 s cluster cap, so clusters get abandoned/restarted and merged; no fixed count is claimed. Merged clusters are > 90 s apart, so at most ~15 fit -> jitter 0..15; none may start in the clean live parts (so none can be longer than the garbage); replays 0, gaps 0; whole pipeline < 10 s.
